model.limitations_text: This model was trained on a survey sample (EICV7) and works at district level. Its accuracy is imperfect and it does not identify real households. Receiving support can itself change a household's welfare. Use it as a policy design tool, not as a list of individuals.

equity.title: Who is reached?
equity.description: Each rule picks households nationwide up to the programmes' actual coverage ({budget_share} of households); the table shows the share of each group's poor households that is reached.
equity.gain_b: Rule B gain per 1,000 poor (95% interval)
equity.interpretation_note: Ranking by poverty risk does not reach every group equally. Where observed targeting already reaches a group better than average, the rules add little. Test the scorecard alongside existing criteria, not as a replacement.

method.what_body: Reach is a policy design tool that audits which poor households are missed by social protection support in Rwanda. It compares existing targeting with model-ranked and transparent scorecard rules using weighted survey estimates, not household records.
method.data_body: {n_households} households in {n_districts} districts, {n_strata} strata and {n_clusters} clusters, from the {survey} survey. Rates, shares and weighted counts are survey-weighted so they describe Rwanda, not only the sample; sample sizes are unweighted counts. Persons: {persons_poor} poor, {persons_extreme_poor} extremely poor.
method.read_body: Every estimate has a 95% interval. If two intervals overlap, the difference is not clear. The small-sample badge means fewer than 30 poor households or fewer than 10 supported households.
method.rule_findings: At the programmes’ own coverage ({budget_share}), observed targeting reaches {observed} of poor households. Rule B reaches {b_reached_interval} (gain {b_gain} per 1,000 poor households, 95% interval {b_interval}); the scorecard reaches {c_reached_interval} (gain {c_gain}, 95% interval {c_interval}). Rule B clearly beats observed targeting in {b_districts} of {n_districts} districts and Rule C in {c_districts}.
method.sensitivity_reach: Poor households reached at observed coverage
method.sensitivity_3: Housing, water, energy and livestock only
method.limit_district: Results are available at district level only.
method.limit_programme_counts: Programme counts are small, so “any support” is the headline measure.
method.limit_extreme_poverty: Extreme poverty estimates are noisy by district.
method.limit_reverse_causality: Support can raise consumption, so exclusion can be understated and leakage overstated.
method.limit_survey_label: Programmes select households by their own criteria; the rules are judged against the survey’s poverty label.
method.limit_individuals: The tool cannot identify real households.
method.limit_financial_inclusion: Financial inclusion is measured generously: any household member counts, and mobile money is included.
method.definition_any_support: Receipt of direct support, classic public works, expanded public works, or nutrition-sensitive direct support.
method.definition_exclusion_error: The share of poor households that receive no support.
method.definition_leakage: The share of supported households that are not poor.
method.definition_triple_gap: The share of households that are poor, receive no support, and have no access to formal financial services.
method.definition_financially_excluded: No household member has a formal financial account or access to a financial service; mobile money is counted as access.

brief.index_body: Choose a district to open its policy brief. Districts are listed by the number of poor households with no support.
brief.unknown_body: We could not find “{district}” in the district estimates. Choose a district from the picker above.
brief.meaning_above: In {district}, the estimated exclusion error is {district_value}, above the national benchmark of {national_value}; the district interval does not include that benchmark.
brief.meaning_below: In {district}, the estimated exclusion error is {district_value}, below the national benchmark of {national_value}; the district interval does not include that benchmark.
brief.meaning_similar: In {district}, the district and national 95% exclusion-error intervals overlap, so the difference is not clear (district value: {district_value}; national value: {national_value}).
brief.action_targeting: Review the targeting criteria: exclusion error is clearly above the national benchmark.
brief.action_access: Pair support with savings groups or mobile-money access: the triple-gap share is clearly above the national benchmark.
brief.action_screening: Test the scorecard as a screening aid alongside existing criteria: model-ranked or scorecard targeting clearly improves reach at observed coverage.
brief.action_small_cell: Collect more data and interpret this district’s figures with care because the sample is small.
brief.action_review: Review targeting criteria only where the exclusion error is clearly above the national value.
brief.nearest_note: The three closest districts are ranked by combined distance in poverty, exclusion error and financial access.
brief.simulator_title: At current coverage: reach per 1,000 poor households
brief.simulator_note: Gain and interval are taken from the simulator’s observed-coverage comparison.
brief.limitations: Limitations: district-level survey estimates; small samples; not a list of real households. Receiving support can change a household’s welfare.
brief.action_monitor: Monitor coverage as new data arrives.
brief.action_outreach: Review local enrolment and service-access barriers with community partners.
brief.action_evaluate: Track whether programme reach and household welfare change over time.
brief.action_review2: Monitor coverage as new data arrives.
brief.action_review3: Review local enrolment and service-access barriers with community partners.
brief.action_screening_both: Test the scorecard as a screening aid alongside existing criteria: both model-ranked and scorecard targeting clearly improve reach at observed coverage.
brief.action_screening_model: Test model-ranked targeting as a screening aid alongside existing criteria: it clearly improves reach at observed coverage.
brief.action_screening_scorecard: Test the scorecard as a screening aid alongside existing criteria: it clearly improves reach at observed coverage.
